messages:
j.doe (Acme): Hey, we saw a spike in latency this morning and several completions came back truncated and weird — lots of garbled tokens. Happens around 2024-11-07 09:12 UTC. Request id: req_9b2f. We pinned model=redwood-14b-reg-v1 and region=us-east but responses look like a smaller model.

maria (Support): Thanks for reporting — sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal curl and the response snippet? Also include headers X-Request-ID / X-Account-ID if available.

j.doe (Acme): Minimal repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \\n  -H 'X-Account-ID: acme-42' \\n  -H 'X-Region: us-east' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-14b-reg-v1","input":"Summarize: The quarterly earnings...","max_tokens":200}'
```
Response snippet: `{"id":"resp_abc","model":"redwood-13b-quant-v1","output":"� ... incomplete summary ..."}`
Also saw a warning in logs: `tokenizer mismatch: vocab size 50256 vs 50260`

maria (Support): :eyes: That looks like the request was routed to redwood-13b-quant-v1 (quantized variant) not the pinned reg-v1. Sam @oncall and Lee from runtime looped in.

sam (Oncall): I see an incident earlier at 09:10 UTC — us-east had a transient capacity overload and our smart router triggered failover. Policy is to fall back to compatible variants, but it should never change model family semantics. Looks like the router matched on "latency-friendly variant" rather than capability. Investigating routing decision for req_9b2f.

lee (EngRuntime): Repro steps I ran: set X-Region=us-east, force model pin redwood-14b-reg-v1, then simulate capacity pressure. Router pick log: `chosen_node: eu-west-1, model_variant: redwood-13b-quant-v1, fallback_reason: capacity`. Bug: compatibility check only looked at architecture and quantization flag, not tokenizer/config hash. So a quantized 13B slipped through.

maria (Support): Customer impact: responses shorter, content omitted, and billing shows tokens billed at quantized model rates (different unit). Acme is upset. Can we prioritize a safe rollback or quick mitigation?

lee (EngRuntime): Mitigation: temporary policy change to enforce strict model_family pin for failovers and to refuse cross-family variant substitution. Pushing a config to router: `failover.strict_family = true`. Also adding server-side check to compare tokenizer hash (sha256) before routing.

sam (Oncall): I've applied the strict_family toggle in prod for the affected routers at 09:26 UTC. Monitoring. Please confirm if Acme still sees wrong model.

maria (Support): I emailed Acme with the mitigation steps and asked for timestamps to verify. Also opened billing ticket to review the charge delta.

j.doe (Acme): Thanks — after 09:28 UTC responses look right again, model field shows `redwood-14b-reg-v1`. Will send a full dump if anything else pops up. Appreciate the speedy response.

lee (EngRuntime): Follow-ups: We need to backfill a regression test in the router suite that verifies tokenizer/config hash match on any fallback variant, and add an alert when region failover picks a different model_family. I'll create an RFC and a small eval harness.

deploy-bot: deploy commit 7f9a3d -> router-config (failover.strict_family=true) succeeded (09:26 UTC).

maria (Support): Closing loop once billing confirms credits. Thanks all.
